verses.text: In the second year of his rule, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams. His mind was troubled, and he could not sleep.
So the king called for the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and astrologers to tell him what he had dreamed. They came in and stood before the king.
The king said to them, "I had a dream, and it troubles me. I want to know what it was."
The astrologers answered the king in Aramaic, "May the king live forever! Tell us, your servants, the dream, and we will explain what it means."

The king answered the astrologers, "I have firmly decided this: If you do not tell me what my dream was and what it means, you will be cut into pieces, and your houses will be turned into piles of rubble.
But if you tell me the dream and explain it, you will receive gifts, rewards, and great honor from me. So tell me the dream and what it means."
Once again they answered, "Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will explain what it means."
The king answered, "I know for certain that you are trying to buy time, because you see that I have firmly decided this.

If you do not tell me the dream, there is only one punishment for you. You have agreed among yourselves to tell me lies and wicked things, hoping the situation will change. So tell me the dream, and then I will know that you can explain what it means."
The astrologers answered the king, "No one on earth can do what the king asks! No king, however great and powerful, has ever asked such a thing of any magician, enchanter, or astrologer.
What the king asks is too hard. No one can tell it to the king except the gods, and they do not live among people."
This made the king so angry and furious that he ordered all the wise men of Babylon to be killed.
So the order went out to kill the wise men, and men were sent to look for Daniel and his friends to kill them too.
Arioch, the commander of the king's guard, had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon. Daniel spoke to him wisely and carefully.
He asked Arioch, the king's officer, "Why did the king give such a harsh order?" Then Arioch explained the matter to Daniel.
So Daniel went in to the king and asked for time, so that he could explain the dream to him.
Then Daniel went home and told his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah what had happened.
He urged them to ask the God of heaven for mercy about this mystery, so that he and his friends would not be killed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
That night the mystery was shown to Daniel in a vision. Then Daniel praised the God of heaven.
Daniel said, "Praise the name of God forever and ever. Wisdom and power belong to him.
He changes times and seasons. He removes kings and puts others in their place. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who understand.
He reveals deep and hidden things. He knows what lies in the darkness, and light lives with him.
I thank you and praise you, God of my ancestors. You have given me wisdom and power. You have shown me what we asked of you. You have shown us what the king wanted to know."

Then Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to kill the wise men of Babylon. He said to him, "Do not kill the wise men of Babylon. Take me to the king, and I will explain his dream to him."
Arioch quickly took Daniel to the king and said, "I have found a man among the captives from Judah who can tell the king what his dream means."
The king asked Daniel, who was also called Belteshazzar, "Can you tell me what I saw in my dream and what it means?"
Daniel answered the king, "No wise man, enchanter, magician, or fortune-teller can explain to the king the mystery he has asked about.

But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries. He has shown King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the days to come. This was your dream, the visions that passed through your mind as you lay in bed:
"Your Majesty, as you were lying there, your thoughts turned to what would happen in the future. The one who reveals mysteries showed you what is going to happen.
As for me, this mystery was not shown to me because I am wiser than anyone else alive. It was shown to me so that you, Your Majesty, would know what it means and understand the thoughts of your mind.
"Your Majesty, you looked, and there in front of you stood a huge statue. It was enormous and dazzling, and it looked terrifying.
The head of the statue was made of pure gold. Its chest and arms were silver. Its belly and thighs were bronze.
Its legs were iron, and its feet were partly iron and partly baked clay.
While you were watching, a rock was cut out, but not by human hands. It struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and smashed them.

Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were all broken to pieces at the same time. They became like chaff on a threshing floor in summer. The wind swept them away without leaving a trace. But the rock that struck the statue became a huge mountain and filled the whole earth.
"That was the dream. Now we will tell the king what it means.
Your Majesty, you are the king of kings. The God of heaven has given you the kingdom, the power, the strength, and the glory.
Wherever people live, he has put them under your control, along with the wild animals and the birds of the sky. He has made you ruler over them all. You are that head of gold.
"After you, another kingdom will rise, weaker than yours. Then a third kingdom, one of bronze, will rule over the whole earth.
Finally, there will be a fourth kingdom, strong as iron. Just as iron breaks and smashes everything, it will crush and break all the others.
You saw that the feet and toes were partly baked clay and partly iron. So this will be a divided kingdom. Yet it will have some of the strength of iron, just as you saw iron mixed with clay.
As the toes were partly iron and partly clay, so this kingdom will be partly strong and partly weak.
And just as you saw iron mixed with clay, the people will mix together through marriage, but they will not stay united, just as iron does not mix with clay.

"In the time of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed. It will never be handed over to another people. It will crush all those kingdoms and bring them to an end, but it will last forever.

This is the meaning of the rock you saw cut out of a mountain, but not by human hands, the rock that broke the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold to pieces. The great God has shown the king what will happen in the future. The dream is true, and its meaning is certain."
Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell face down before Daniel and honored him. He ordered that an offering and incense be presented to him.
The king said to Daniel, "Truly your God is the God of gods and the Lord of kings. He reveals mysteries, because you were able to reveal this mystery."
Then the king gave Daniel a high position and many great gifts. He made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon and put him in charge of all its wise men.
At Daniel's request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to run the affairs of the province of Babylon, while Daniel himself stayed at the king's court.
